title: Sequential approximate isometries: multiplicative mass and target-error growth
question:
Let \(n\ge0\) and let \(H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}\) with finite \(d_j\ge1\). Core \(j\) is a linear map
\[
V_j:H_{j-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb C^2\otimes H_j\qquad(1\le j\le n).
\]
All spaces carry their standard Euclidean inner products; \(\dagger\) means conjugate transpose and \(\|\cdot\|_{\rm op}\) is the induced operator norm. Rows label outputs and columns label inputs. A new bit is appended after all previously emitted bits, and the bond remains the final tensor factor. Put \(T_0=I_{H_0}\) and, using only the corresponding norm-preserving regrouping,
\[
T_j=(I_{(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes(j-1)}}\otimes V_j)T_{j-1}.
\]
Assume the local Gram defects satisfy
\[
\|V_j^\dagger V_j-I_{H_{j-1}}\|_{\rm op}\le\eta_j,
\qquad 0\le\eta_j<1.
\]
These are approximate linear maps; neither full unitary completions nor a physical channel realization is assumed.

1. Prove a one-step norm-squared inequality valid for every vector on passive emitted bits and the incoming bond, including vectors entangled between those factors. Use it to derive, for every \(v\in H_0\) and every length \(n\),
\[
\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\eta_j)\|v\|_2^2
\le\|T_n v\|_2^2\le
\prod_{j=1}^n(1+\eta_j)\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Give the resulting bound on \(\|T_n^\dagger T_n-I\|_{\rm op}\). Show that the two mass endpoints can each be attained by legal bond-dimension-one trains. Do not replace the product by \(1\pm\sum_j\eta_j\) as an exact general inequality without justification.

2. Does zero defect at every stage imply fidelity to a specified target train? Give two legal one-stage, bond-dimension-one trains with zero defects whose outputs from initial scalar 1 are orthogonal. State exactly what Gram/mass control therefore certifies and what target information it lacks.

3. In this separate comparison branch, suppose additional maps \(W_j:H_{j-1}\to\mathbb C^2\otimes H_j\) are exact isometries, \(W_j^\dagger W_j=I\), and \(\|V_j-W_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j\) with \(\epsilon_j\ge0\). Let \(S_n\) be their sequential composition in the same order as \(T_n\). For a unit vector \(v\), prove the growth-weighted target bound
\[
\|T_n v-S_n v\|_2
\le\sum_{k=1}^n\epsilon_k\prod_{j=k+1}^n\sqrt{1+\eta_j}.
\]
Explain why the product weights involve stages later than the inserted discrepancy. Give a two-stage, bond-dimension-one example satisfying all stated premises for which the simpler claim \(\|T_2v-S_2v\|_2\le\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2\) fails. This is an unnormalized vector bound; no normalization or postselection is implicit.

4. Check the empty chain, zero input, and the exact-isometry specialization. Separately replace the strict local condition by \(\eta_j=1\) and show why a positive lower mass is then not guaranteed. Explain why these conclusions alone give neither a unitary-circuit synthesis theorem nor terminal-bond cleanup. Each diagnostic must state which premises it retains or replaces.

assumptions: Finite nonzero complex bond spaces with standard Euclidean inner products and dimension-compatible core maps.

Only the comparison branch receives exact ideal isometries W_j and operator differences bounded by epsilon_j; unit input is required only for its displayed absolute error budget.
The eta_j=1 diagnostic replaces the strict defect premise; the zero-input diagnostic does not retain the comparison branch unit-input premise.
conventions: Each core maps an incoming column vector to a new-bit and outgoing-bond column vector; emitted bits are ordered chronologically and the bond is last.
Adjoint is conjugate transpose; all norms are induced Euclidean norms and the tensor regrouping is norm-preserving.
Gram control concerns unnormalized linear maps; it does not by itself define a physical probability-preserving channel or clean terminal register.
All empty products equal one and empty sums equal zero.

mathematical_target: Prove all-length multiplicative mass control and sharpness for sequential approximately isometric cores; separate target fidelity, derive its growth-weighted comparison bound under additional local alignment premises, and refute the naive additive bound.
reference_answer:
Let \(D_j=V_j^\dagger V_j-I\). This operator is Hermitian, and for every incoming bond vector \(z\), Cauchy–Schwarz and the induced norm give
\[
\big|\|V_jz\|_2^2-\|z\|_2^2\big|
=|\langle z,D_jz\rangle|
\le\eta_j\|z\|_2^2.
\]
Thus \((1-\eta_j)\|z\|^2\le\|V_jz\|^2\le(1+\eta_j)\|z\|^2\). To retain entangled prefixes, choose an orthonormal basis \(\{e_p\}\) of the already-emitted-bit space and write an arbitrary vector as \(y=\sum_pe_p\otimes z_p\). The vectors \(z_p\) need not be proportional or normalized. Orthogonality of the prefix labels gives
\[
\|y\|^2=\sum_p\|z_p\|^2,
\qquad\|(I\otimes V_j)y\|^2=\sum_p\|V_jz_p\|^2.
\]
Sum the bond inequalities to obtain the same factors \(1\pm\eta_j\) for every such \(y\). The basis regrouping in the question changes no norm. This proof does not assume the state factors between prefix and bond.

Apply that one-step bound to \(y=T_{j-1}v\). Since every \(1-\eta_j\) is positive, forward induction from \(T_0=I\) gives
\[
a_n\|v\|^2\le\|T_nv\|^2\le b_n\|v\|^2,
\quad a_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1-\eta_j),\quad b_n=\prod_{j=1}^n(1+\eta_j).
\]
Equivalently \(a_nI\preceq T_n^\dagger T_n\preceq b_nI\). Diagonalize the finite-dimensional Hermitian operator \(T_n^\dagger T_n-I\): its eigenvalues belong to \([a_n-1,b_n-1]\). Therefore
\[
\|T_n^\dagger T_n-I\|_{\rm op}
\le\max\{1-a_n,b_n-1\}.
\]
One may simplify the maximum to \(b_n-1\): expansion of \(\prod(1+\eta_j)+\prod(1-\eta_j)\) contains twice the nonnegative even-degree elementary terms, including 1, so it is at least 2. The maximum form already proves the requested certificate. No replacement of \(b_n\) by \(1+\sum\eta_j\) is valid in general, because the positive cross terms are then lost. A weaker lower estimate \(a_n\ge1-\sum\eta_j\) is valid for \(0\le\eta_j\le1\), but may be nonpositive and is not needed.

For endpoint sharpness take every bond dimension one and let \(V_j^\pm z=\sqrt{1\pm\eta_j}\,z|0\rangle\), retaining the one-dimensional bond. Its local Gram operator is \((1\pm\eta_j)I\), so its defect is exactly \(\eta_j\). On initial scalar 1 the complete output is \(\prod_j\sqrt{1\pm\eta_j}\,|0\cdots0\rangle\), whose squared norm is exactly \(b_n\) for the plus train or \(a_n\) for the minus train. These are two legal trains, each attaining the corresponding endpoint; no claim is made that a single scalar train simultaneously attains unequal endpoints. In particular the upper global Gram bound can be attained.

Mass preservation does not identify a target. For \(n=1\) with one-dimensional input and terminal bonds, take \(V_1z=z|0\rangle\) and \(W_1z=z|1\rangle\). Both have Gram operator \([1]\), yet their outputs from 1 have inner product zero and Euclidean distance \(\sqrt2\), even after an arbitrary global phase is attached to either output. Their pure-state overlap fidelity is zero. Gram checks control how the map distorts input norms and inner products; they contain no alignment information with a specified emitted target vector or train. This obstruction uses no nonzero defect at all.

Now retain the additional hypotheses in the comparison branch. Write the lifted, regrouped maps as \(A_j=I\otimes V_j\) and \(B_j=I\otimes W_j\). The same prefix decomposition proves \(\|A_j\|_{\rm op}\le\sqrt{1+\eta_j}\), that \(B_j\) is an exact isometry, and that \(\|A_j-B_j\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_j\). The last assertion follows by applying \(\|(V_j-W_j)z_p\|\le\epsilon_j\|z_p\|\), squaring and summing; it is valid on entangled inputs as well. Hence \(\|S_{j-1}v\|=1\) when \(\|v\|=1\).

Set \(q_j=\|T_jv-S_jv\|\). Then \(q_0=0\), and the exact difference identity is
\[
T_jv-S_jv=A_j(T_{j-1}v-S_{j-1}v)+(A_j-B_j)S_{j-1}v.
\]
The triangle inequality yields
\[
q_j\le\sqrt{1+\eta_j}\,q_{j-1}+\epsilon_j.
\]
Induction unrolls this forward recurrence as
\[
q_n\le\sum_{k=1}^n\epsilon_k\prod_{j=k+1}^n\sqrt{1+\eta_j}.
\]
The discrepancy inserted at stage \(k\) is applied to an exact ideal prefix of norm one. It is subsequently propagated through the actual later maps \(V_{k+1},\ldots,V_n\), explaining precisely the later-stage weights. A telescoping expansion with ideal later maps would use different, earlier-stage growth factors; it must not be mixed with this recurrence.

The simple additive replacement fails even in dimension one. Use two stages, \(v=1\), \(W_jz=z|0\rangle\), and \(V_jz=(5/4)z|0\rangle\). Then
\[
\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=1/4,\qquad
\eta_1=\eta_2=(5/4)^2-1=9/16<1.
\]
These are exact local operator differences and Gram defects. The output difference is
\[
\|(25/16)|00\rangle-|00\rangle\|=9/16>1/2=\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2.
\]
The stated weighted bound is \((1/4)(5/4)+1/4=9/16\), so it is attained in this example. The norm of the actual output is \(25/16\); this is exactly why ordinary unitary telescoping cannot be imported unchanged. Nothing here identifies an unnormalized linear action with a physical channel.

For \(n=0\), \(T_0=S_0=I\), both products are one, the global Gram defect is zero and the comparison sum is zero. For the zero input \(v=0\), linearity makes both outputs zero and the mass inequalities hold with equality; this replaces the comparison branch's unit-input premise rather than asserting that zero is a unit vector. When all \(\eta_j=0\), every \(V_j\) is an exact isometry, the mass is preserved and the weighted comparison bound reduces to \(\sum_j\epsilon_j\); target fidelity still needs the comparison hypotheses, as the orthogonal example shows.

For the requested strictness diagnostic replace one local restriction by \(\eta_j=1\). With one-dimensional bonds and \(n=1\), take \(V_1=0\); then \(\|V_1^\dagger V_1-I\|=1\) but the output from 1 has zero mass. The nonnegative lower factor becomes zero, so the positive lower-mass conclusion is lost. This witness is outside the original strict \(\eta_j<1\) regime. Under that original regime a supplied map is injective, which already forces \(d_{j-1}\le2d_j\); the proof does not assert existence of such maps for incompatible dimensions.

Finally, rectangular approximate maps with norm gain are not themselves unitary gates. A unitary realization, a finite gate set and its approximation cost, and a physical preparation mechanism would need separate constructions. Nor does norm preservation force a chosen terminal bond label: an exact one-stage isometry may output \(|0\rangle\otimes|1\rangle\) in a two-dimensional terminal bond while the desired clean label is \(|0\rangle\). Thus the theorem retains the entire terminal bond and proves neither its cleanup nor a synthesis result.

rubric.criterion: Derives the local quadratic-form bounds from the Hermitian Gram defect (1), and extends them to all passive-prefix inputs by a valid orthogonal-block, spectral or tensor-operator argument without assuming a product state (1).

Proves the all-length lower/upper mass products, including the empty base and positivity of the lower factors (1); deduces the global operator Gram norm bound from all-vector/Hermitian control (0.5); gives legal scalar trains attaining each endpoint (0.5). An unsupported replacement by an additive upper mass bound loses the affected credit.

Provides and computes a defect-zero pair with orthogonal outputs (0.5), and clearly distinguishes norm/inner-product control from target alignment (0.5). A mere global-phase example is insufficient for the expressly requested orthogonal witness.

In the separate comparison branch, justifies spectator-stable bounds for V_j-W_j and exact ideal-prefix norm one (0.5), derives the ordered difference recurrence (1), and proves the requested sum with later-stage growth products (1). May use an equivalent telescoping proof if it produces the stated bound and preserves all additional hypotheses.

Supplies an actual two-stage example satisfying eta_j<1 and the local epsilon bounds, computes an output error greater than epsilon_1+epsilon_2, and explains the nonisometric growth. The rational 5/4 example is not required specifically.

Handles n=0, v=0 and eta=0 in their proper scopes (0.5); gives a legal eta=1 zero-output diagnostic while explicitly replacing the strict premise (0.5); and distinguishes the retained terminal bond and approximate linear maps from physical unitary synthesis/cleanup claims (0.5).

common_errors: Assuming prefix/bond product structure and omitting entangled inputs.
Replacing the multiplicative upper mass bound by 1+sum eta without its positive cross terms.
Inferring target fidelity from exact local orthogonality or normalization.
Applying unitary telescoping to V_j while its norm can exceed one.
Placing earlier-stage rather than later-stage growth weights in the stated recurrence proof.
Using the comparison result without an ideal isometry supplier and local target alignment.
Treating eta=1 or v=0 counterexamples as satisfying strict-defect or unit-input premises.
Identifying an unnormalized linear action with a physical deterministic channel or asserting terminal cleanup from mass alone.

boundary_cases.resolution: Both compositions are identities, mass factors are one and comparison error is zero.
Mass equality and zero outputs hold by linearity; this does not satisfy the comparison branch unit-input premise.
Mass is exact and target-error weights are one, but target alignment remains a separate condition.
Replace eta<1 by eta=1; the zero map can annihilate a nonzero input, so positive lower mass fails.
Eta<1 implies injectivity and therefore d_{j-1}<=2d_j; supplied-map premises have no realization otherwise.
The entire terminal bond remains part of the output; norm control does not select a clean label.

steps.justification: D=V^dagger V-I is Hermitian; Cauchy-Schwarz bounds |<z,Dz>| by eta||z||^2.

steps.claim: Preserve the inequalities under passive prefixes, including entangled states.
steps.conclusion: The same bounds hold for I_prefix tensor V_j on every prefix/bond vector; its norm is <=sqrt(1+eta_j).
steps.justification: Expand y=sum_p e_p tensor z_p in an orthonormal prefix basis and sum squared norms. No factorization of y is assumed.
Forward induction from T_0=I, multiplying nonnegative local factors.

steps.claim: Convert all-vector mass control to global operator Gram control.
steps.justification: The Hermitian quadratic-form bounds locate every eigenvalue; the optional simplification uses the nonnegative even-degree expansion.

steps.conclusion: Dimension-one maps V_j^plus/minus z=sqrt(1 plus/minus eta_j) z|0> attain b_n/a_n respectively.
steps.justification: Compute each scalar Gram defect and the product amplitude. These are separate witnesses, not simultaneous endpoints of one scalar map.

steps.claim: Refute target fidelity from Gram tests.
steps.conclusion: V z=z|0> and W z=z|1> both have zero defect and orthogonal outputs from 1.
steps.justification: Direct inner product and norm computation. The exact-isometry property is checked for this witness; no zero local-target difference is assumed.

steps.claim: Supply all comparison operator bounds on the actual spaces.
steps.conclusion: Lifted actual maps have norm <=sqrt(1+eta_j), lifted differences have norm <=epsilon_j, and ||S_jv||=1.
steps.justification: Repeat the orthogonal-prefix argument for V_j-W_j; exact ideal isometries preserve the unit initial norm.

steps.claim: Derive and unroll the ordered comparison recurrence.

steps.justification: Insert A_j(T_{j-1}-S_{j-1})+(A_j-B_j)S_{j-1}; the actual later maps propagate each inserted discrepancy.

steps.justification: Compute both Grams, local differences and the two-stage output explicitly. All comparison premises are verified for this example.

steps.justification: Definitions and linearity; this node does not retain the comparison unit-input premise.

steps.claim: Check comparison empty-chain and exact-isometry specializations.
steps.conclusion: For n=0 the comparison error is zero; if every eta_j=0 then growth factors are one and the comparison bound is sum epsilon_j.
steps.justification: Empty sum or substitution in the already proved bound; alignment hypotheses remain present.

steps.claim: Demonstrate loss of strict lower mass at defect one.
assumptions: G2-I6 replaces G2-I2 for this witness; do not assume eta<1.
steps.conclusion: With n=1 and scalar bonds V=0 has defect one and sends initial 1 to zero.
steps.justification: Compute V^dagger V-I=-I; the lower factor is zero.

steps.conclusion: The mathematics is a bound on full emitted vectors retaining the terminal bond; neither unitary synthesis nor a chosen clean label follows.
steps.justification: The expanding scalar witness is not a unitary column; even an exact isometry can put terminal amplitude on a non-clean label. Under eta<1 supplied maps must be injective, so incompatible dimensions are unrealizable.
